To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have identified the cubic donor - bound exciton and donor - acceptor emission bands in the photoluminescence spectra of GaN grown on c-plane sappire, that the cubic contents in GaN layers on sapphire are strongly dependent on the growth temperature and the growth time and that the cubic contents can be reduced by using a high growth temperature and a short growth time.
the cubic content of GaN on sapphires can be controlled by growth conditions.
we observe two emission bands from GaN grown on sapphire, which are identified as the donor bound excitonic recombination and the donor - acceptor pair recombination in cubic GaN.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structural and optical properties of GaN grown on c-plane sapphires.
the structural and optical properties of cubic GaN on sappire.
the epitaxial growth and the structural properties of GaN on sapphir, and the optical properties of cubic GaN.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cubic phase is a metastable phase and the growth of GaN on saphire leads to the formation of cubic GaN in the upper layers of the GaN film.
the cubic GaN is not a problem for the growth of high quality layers.
cubic GaN inclusions in GaN on sapphires are unavoidable and that the cubic content in the top region of the layers is strongly dependent on growth conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cubic content is a function of the GaN growth temperature.
the cubic content of GaN on saphire is not a problem as long as the growth is optimized and the layer thickness is kept below 400 nm.
we have shown a way to control the formation of cubic GaN.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cubic phase can be controlled by proper choice of growth parameters.
the cubic phase of GaN is not an unwanted contaminant in the growth process but can be used for optical applications.
the optical density measurements are very useful for determining the cubic content and for the analysis of the optical properties of GaN on sapphires.
